name: upgrade-deck-vs-library
body: Detection and the two version anchors. `kalide upgrade` operates on the current directory with no path argument (mirroring `kalide init`): it is a deck if `kalide.yaml` is present (deck-config), a template library if `library.yaml` is present (domain.value.library-manifest). Both present, or neither, is an error and nothing is written [autonomous]. The two kinds have different anchors: a library is versioned by the required `library.yaml` `format:` integer — today only `1` is accepted, because internal/template.loadLibraryMeta rejects every other value, so nothing today can actually be at another format — whereas a deck's `kalide.yaml` has no version field at all (its key set is title, author, date, theme, navigation, properties, templates), so no deck format migration exists today and the deck migration path is a no-op. A deck's kalide-owned files are recognized by content only in the refresh half, against the known-version catalog (global.constraint.upgrade-known-version-catalog); no deck version is ever invented for migration [autonomous]. The running binary's implemented format — the basis for "newer" — is the highest `library.yaml` format the binary implements, today `1`; a `dev`/unstamped build implements the same format as the source it was built from, so the comparison is on the format integer, not on the `main.version` string, and `dev` never means "newer". The running binary's version is `main.version` (stamped via -ldflags -X, `dev` otherwise), the same value `kalide version` prints (version-command) [autonomous]. The command surface (`kalide upgrade`, no `--force`), the two-half scope (refresh + migrate) and the conservative never-clobber safety model are the user's firm decisions [with user].
